title: Synthetic SITF cross-component attack flows
claim_boundary: These are repository-owned synthetic review scenarios composed from pinned SITF technique identifiers. They are not upstream Wiz Research flows, observed incidents, or proof of complete attack-path mitigation.

flows.title: Developer endpoint to poisoned production image
flows.scenario: An attacker compromises a developer endpoint, steals source authority, changes protected source, executes in CI, and attempts to promote a malicious image.

steps.objective: Execute attacker-controlled code on the developer endpoint.
Harvest locally available credentials and tokens.
Use stolen credentials to access the source platform.
Modify protected source or workflow content.
Run malicious code in the workflow context.
Attempt to obtain additional workflow secrets.
Publish an attacker-controlled container image.
Move the poisoned image into production.

flows.title: Cross-fork poisoned pipeline to production network
flows.scenario: An attacker abuses fork object identity and pipeline promotion, poisons shared state, persists on a runner, and pivots toward production.

steps.objective: Confuse trusted and fork-controlled object identity.
Trigger privileged behavior from an untrusted pull request.
Poison reusable action or build cache state.
Persist on a self-hosted runner across jobs.
Use runner network reachability to approach production.

flows.title: Malicious package to release and deployment credentials
flows.scenario: An attacker introduces a deceptive package that executes during build, steals registry authority, and tries to replace a trusted production image.

steps.objective: Present a typosquatted package name.
Exploit namespace or resolver confusion.
Execute code through a package lifecycle script.
Run the malicious package on a CI runner.
Steal registry publication credentials.
Publish a malicious image under trusted naming.
Attempt to admit the malicious image to production.

flows.title: Workflow prompt injection to malicious deployment
flows.scenario: Untrusted pull-request content manipulates an AI-enabled workflow into changing source, opening a pull request, and initiating a deployment.

steps.objective: Inject instructions through untrusted workflow input.
Cause the workflow to modify repository content.
Persist malicious code in protected source.
Create or promote a pull request from the compromised workflow.
Attempt deployment through the compromised pipeline.
